notes: DEGRADED TELEMETRY / CLOCK SKEW (adversarial, first clock_skew scenario). Culprit is 'perf(session-cache): approximate LFU eviction' (authored 09:05, deployed to session-cache 09:20): it replaces an LRU cache (which structurally protects hot keys, since both Get and Set call MoveToFront) with a hand-rolled sampled-LFU evictor (sample size 3), but the diff contains a silent frequency-tracking bug that is never announced in prose: the new Set() unconditionally does `c.freq[key] = 1` on every write (including refresh-writes of an already-present key) and the new Get() never touches c.freq at all (`val, ok := c.items[key]; return val, ok`, no increment). Reading the diff literally, `c.freq[key]` is assigned exactly once, always to 1, and never incremented anywhere — so every key's frequency is permanently 1, forever, regardless of how often it is actually read. evictOne()'s 'least-frequency of 3 samples' therefore degenerates into uniform-random eviction among 3 sampled keys, since the first sample's freq(1) is never strictly less than a later sample's freq(1). The old LRU never had this failure mode: MoveToFront on both Get and Set kept hot keys structurally at the front, safe from the tail-eviction pointer. Under Zipfian session access (a small number of session keys carry the overwhelming majority of traffic), uniform-random eviction hits hot keys at a rate proportional to their share of the *key space*, not their share of *traffic* — so hot keys get evicted and immediately reloaded, over and over, cratering the hit ratio. cache_hit_ratio ramps 0.96->0.55 and cache_evictions_per_sec ramps 42->820, both from 09:30 (the true incident onset, 10 minutes after the culprit's 09:20 deploy) through 10:30. Downstream, auth-gw's session_lookup_p95_ms ramps 35->1380ms from 09:40 (cache misses force a fallback to the primary session store) and session_lookup_error_ratio ramps from 09:45; frontend's login_latency_p95_ms steps to 2400ms at 09:55 (blast radius). first_failing_service is session-cache; auth-gw and frontend are blast radius. SKEW MECHANISM: [[degradations]] applies clock_skew to LOGS ONLY, service=auth-gw, offset_s=90 — auth-gw's metrics, every trace span (all services), and every other service's logs stay TRUE; only the timestamp field of auth-gw's own log rows is shifted +90s. Detection path has three legs: (1) HEARTBEAT — auth-gw emits a deterministic 'cron heartbeat' INFO log at exactly 1/min (in_patterns=false, so it never surfaces as an alerting pattern and carries zero incident signal of its own); before skew every row lands on a whole minute, but in logs.ndjson every single row instead lands at :30 seconds past the minute — a constant, mechanical 90s offset, unrelated to the incident's timing and diagnostic of clock skew on its own. (2) CROSS-SIGNAL MISMATCH — auth-gw's WARN log_fault ('session lookup slow: falling back to primary store', rate 8/min) is generated to start at true 09:40:00, exactly matching the unskewed session_lookup_p95_ms ramp start, but the +90s shift moves its first row in logs.ndjson to 09:41:30 — a systematic 90-second gap between a service's own logs and its own metric that appears on no other service and cannot be explained by any real causal delay (a real fallback-latency effect would show up in the metric too, not just the log). (3) CONTROL — session-cache is not skewed: its WARN log_fault ('cache miss; evicted key required origin re-fetch', 3/min) starts at exactly 09:30:00, in lockstep with its own cache_hit_ratio/cache_evictions_per_sec ramps, and every hand-written trace exemplar (frontend -> auth-gw -> session-cache, three groups at 09:47:10, 10:15:40, 10:36:50) uses TRUE timestamps that agree with the unskewed session_lookup_p95_ms ramp, not the skewed WARN rows — traces are never skewed, only auth-gw's logs are, so cross-referencing traces or session-cache's own signals against auth-gw's logs exposes exactly which service's telemetry is artifact-shifted. TRAP LOGIC: auth-log-decoy ('feat(auth): structured session claims logging', authored 09:20, deployed to auth-gw at true 09:31 -- only 1 minute after the REAL onset of 09:30, already too late to be causal even at face value) is the mechanism-trap centerpiece. A solver who trusts auth-gw's own logs.ndjson timestamps at face value sees auth-gw's errors apparently starting at 09:41:30, which is 10.5 minutes after the 09:31 deploy -- a suspiciously clean deploy-to-onset gap that closely mirrors the REAL culprit's true gap (session-cache's culprit deployed 09:20, true onset 09:30, a 10-minute gap). The skew manufactures a decoy causal story shaped just like the real one, for the wrong service, purely from a clock artifact. It is exonerated two ways: (a) mechanism -- the diff only adds structured fields (session_id, claims) to an existing log.Info call; it changes no control flow and cannot alter cache behavior or latency; (b) timing -- deploys.json timestamps are never skewed, so even at face value this deploy (09:31) lands after the true onset (09:30), and the actual downstream ramp (session_lookup_p95_ms from 09:40) is fully explained by session-cache's hit-ratio collapse, itself a direct continuation of the 09:20 eviction-policy change. ttl-raise-decoy ('raise session TTL 30m->60m', session-cache, deployed 08:50, PRE-onset -- this is the deploy that satisfies the pre-onset-decoy invariant) is wrong-direction: a longer TTL only extends how long entries survive, which can only improve hit ratio, never collapse it. rwmutex-decoy ('use RWMutex for concurrent reads', session-cache, deployed 09:00, between the two other session-cache decoys and the culprit) is a semantics-preserving concurrency refactor: swapping sync.Mutex for sync.RWMutex with RLock/RUnlock on Get and Lock/Unlock retained on Set/evictOne changes locking granularity only -- it never touches eviction policy, key sampling, or frequency tracking. poolsize-decoy ('raise primary-store connection pool 20->50', auth-gw, deployed 09:50, squarely mid-ramp) is the most dangerous auth-gw-side bait: right service, right neighborhood. Exonerated by wrong direction (a larger connection pool can only increase fallback concurrency/throughput, not cause latency) and by timing (session_lookup_p95_ms already began ramping at 09:40, ten minutes before this deploy). banner-decoy ('refresh session banner copy', frontend, deployed 10:34 -- 6 minutes before fired_at 10:40) is classic innocent-deploy-near-alert bait: a one-line cosmetic copy change in an unrelated file, present purely to satisfy the decoy-position invariant near the alert. 14 deploys_auto entries (>=4 pre-onset, cyclic across all five services) are pure background noise: routine dependency/docs/CI/test tweaks touching none of eviction.go, cache.go, config.go, log.go, or store.go. Patterns are victim-first: auth-gw's WARN pattern (8/min from 09:40 true -> ~1104 total rows) is the loudest incident pattern, ahead of frontend's ERROR pattern (5/min from 09:55 -> ~615) and session-cache's own WARN pattern (3/min from 09:30 -> ~444, the lowest of the three despite being the cause); 3 patterns_extra stale background negatives (kafka rebalancing on billing-worker, disk usage on search-indexer, TLS renewal on frontend; counts 48-70, delta +2) sit below all three incident patterns and are unrelated pre-existing chatter. A search-indexer index_lag_ms spike (baseline ~95 -> 520, 08:05-08:35) self-heals a full 55 minutes before onset and is unrelated red-herring noise on an uninvolved service. Remediation: roll back session-cache to the pre-sampled-LFU build.
